content: Buspirone is a medication prescribed to treat anxiety disorders or to manage symptoms of anxiety for a short duration. It may also be prescribed for other conditions, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Buspirone is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically two or three times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take buspirone exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel better, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, especially if you have been on high doses for an extended period. If discontinuation is necessary, your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually. Note that it may take several weeks of consistent use before the full therapeutic effects of buspirone are observed. In some cases, buspirone is also used to alleviate symptoms associated with premenstrual syndrome (PMS). If you are considering this medication for such purposes, discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Before starting buspirone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to buspirone or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, including antihistamines, anticonvulsants (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin), dexamethasone, diazepam, diltiazem, erythromycin, haloperidol, ketoconazole, itraconazole, MAO inhibitors, muscle relaxants, nefazodone, narcotic pain medications, rifampin, ritonavir, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, trazodone, verapamil, and any vitamins or supplements. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, or if you have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking buspirone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking buspirone. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the sedative effects of buspirone, so it is advisable to avoid consuming alcohol while on this medication. Buspirone can be taken with or without food, but it is important to maintain consistency—either always take it with food or always take it without food. Avoid consuming large quantities of grapefruit juice while taking this medication, as it may interfere with its effectiveness. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is within four hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Buspirone may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, dry mouth, depression, excitement, fatigue, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, lightheadedness, weakness, and numbness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include skin rash, itching, fast or irregular heartbeat, blurred vision, and unusual movements of the head or neck muscles. If you experience any severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store buspirone in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, excessive heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly—consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include upset stomach, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any recommended laboratory tests to monitor your response to buspirone. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Buspirone is sold under the brand names BuSpar® and BuSpar® Dividose.
